questions.text: How are the location, direction, and distance of a place determined?
questions.text_as_printed: How are the location, direction, and distance of a place determined? (D)

answer.value:
Role of Latitudes and Longitudes:
The Earth is spherical, making it difficult to measure location, direction, and distance. Imaginary lines—latitudes (east-west) and longitudes (north-south)—are drawn to measure specific locations, directions, and distances. These geographical coordinates help in precise identification of places.

The 180° longitude is known as the International Date Line, passing through the Pacific Ocean opposite the 0° longitude (Greenwich Meridian). It is drawn in a zigzag pattern to avoid landmasses. Travelers adjust their day and date for convenience when crossing this line.

questions.text: Latitude and longitudes play a significant role in determining the climate of a region. Justify
questions.text_as_printed: Latitude and longitudes play a significant role in determining the climate of a region. Justify (D)

answer.value:
Climatic Zones and Latitudes:
The regions between 23°30' North and South latitudes receive maximum solar heat and are considered the Torrid Zone.
The climate in this zone is hot.
Areas between 23°30' and 66°30' in both hemispheres receive moderate heat and are called the Temperate Zone.
Regions from 66°30' to 90° North and South are considered the Frigid Zone due to low solar heat.
Latitudes and longitudes help determine the climate of a region

questions.text: Write a note on the importance of the International Date Line.
questions.text_as_printed: Write a note on the importance of the International Date Line. (A)

answer.value:
International Date Line:
The 180° longitude is called the International Date Line, passing through the Pacific Ocean opposite the 0° longitude.
It is drawn in a zigzag pattern to avoid landmasses.
Traveling from east to west across this line results in losing one day.
Traveling from west to east results in gaining a day (experiencing the same day twice).
This line helps adjust time and date for travelers.

questions.text: How are latitudes different from longitudes?
questions.text_as_printed: How are latitudes different from longitudes? (A)

answer.value:
Latitudes | Longitudes
Imaginary lines drawn east-west on the globe, parallel to the Equator. | Imaginary lines that intersect the Equator and join the North and South Poles.
The Equator is the 0° great circle, and the circles of latitude become smaller towards the north and south. | All longitudes are equal in length.
Including the Equator, there are a total of 181 latitudes. | There are a total of 360 longitudes.
The distance between one latitude and the next on the Earth's surface is about 110.4 km. | The maximum distance between two longitudes is at the Equator, about 111 km.

Imaginary lines drawn east-west on the globe, parallel to the Equator. | Imaginary lines that intersect the Equator and join the North and South Poles.
The Equator is the 0° great circle, and the circles of latitude become smaller towards the north and south. | All longitudes are equal in length.
Including the Equator, there are a total of 181 latitudes. | There are a total of 360 longitudes.
The distance between one latitude and the next on the Earth's surface is about 110.4 km. | The maximum distance between two longitudes is at the Equator, about 111 km.
